gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-noto-sans-myanmar: Nulshock stretches out wide with spacious tracking and a bold, technical outline as thin as a pipe cleaner. Noto Sans Myanmar sits below it as a thick, heavy-looking strip of text, its c opening broadly.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-noto-sans-nabatae: Noto Sans Nabataean stands its lowercase almost as tall as the capitals, with wide s curves in a plain sans body. Nulshock is the stretched, ribbon-cut display voice; the body does the quiet work.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-noto-sans-nag-mun: Technical from the first line, Nulshock spreads its outlined letters wide, with a lowercase n whose arch and stem match. Noto Sans Nag Mundari follows with half-unwrapped c and s shapes and lowercase that rivals its capitals.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-noto-sans-nandina: Noto Sans Nandinagari has short ascenders, a big lowercase body and openings that stay generous at every weight. Nulshock, in monoline strokes throughout, would lead into it with stretched, bold outlines, so a long stretch of text stays friendly.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-noto-sans-newa: Wide, wiry and bold, Nulshock draws its outlines with no brush-like swelling at all. Noto Sans Newa has a clearly open mouth on the lowercase e and tall counters, which is the pair's sharpest contrast.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-noto-sans-nushu: Modern in feel, Nulshock is tubular and wire-like, stretched wide for impact as a display heading. Noto Sans Nushu has a towering x-height and terminals held far from the stroke body, which suits steady text.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-noto-sans-ogham: Noto Sans Ogham looks bold in its lowercase because the bodies are so tall, with wide gaps in the e. Nulshock's glass-tube lettering is hollow and wide, so a long page stays easy going.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-noto-sans-ol-chik: Hollow, wide and technical, Nulshock reads like outlines drawn in one width. And Noto Sans Ol Chiki holds its curve tails well back, so words form solid blocks; keep its size generous.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-noto-sans-old-hun: Noto Sans Old Hungarian opens its tall a, e and s with large counters, and its apertures stay open at tiny sizes. Nulshock draws a single-weight line like a plotter pen, while Noto Sans Old Hungarian keeps a long read friendly.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-noto-sans-old-ita: Contemporary and sharp, Nulshock draws its stems and connecting strokes with no modulation at all. And Noto Sans Old Italic brings very little gap between x-height and cap height, with curve endings kept well apart.
